Source: `691e9f70ad7a8c071c57b85752a4b8b56b8e4bc6`, observed 2026-10-26 14:06 GMT+7.
Source reads only: no provider queries, endpoint probes, builds, installs, tests,
Git mutations, or Finance control-plane activity were performed by this helper.

## Scope and counts

`infra/cloudflare/edge-security/inventory/source-census.jsonl` contains **1,824 app route entry files across 30 apps**, **461 Web
legacy implementation files**, and **1,375 client path literal records** from
`packages/sdk`, `packages/internal-api`, and `apps/mobile/lib`.
The total 2,285 route source files is not a unique deployed endpoint count.
Web wrappers point to legacy implementations; generated HEAD wrappers share a
GET implementation. Multiple hosts can expose the same shared implementation.
All app entries have path, methods, source, implementation, host candidate,
caller class, auth signals or an explicit unknown, and evidence references.

The generator is `scripts/edge-security-inventory.py`, invoked from the repository root:

```sh
python3 scripts/edge-security-inventory.py --root . \
  --dns-snapshot infra/cloudflare/edge-security/inventory/hosts.json \
  --output infra/cloudflare/edge-security/inventory/source-census.jsonl
```

This is a census, not an exhaustive authorization audit. **563 app entries are explicitly tagged as generic auth unknowns** after resolving shallow route forwarding. Bootstrap, public, and metadata route conventions also need handler-specific validation when no direct signal is present.
They are explicitly unknown, not proven unauthenticated. Direct helper signals
likewise do not prove every method checks actor/workspace permissions. Imports
through framework aliases, computed router handlers, runtime configuration, and
dynamic path construction require manual interpretation. The source is large;
the manually traced machine contracts below are the basis for proposed traffic
classes. The paused Rust backend and TanStack Web are excluded from execution
and from this Next route census; their retained source was not refreshed.

from the parent's read-only provider inventory. A custom domain is not covered by
the tuturuuu.com zone. Registry-only hosts docs, qr, mira, colab, and the separately
configured realtime/control services must not disappear because they lack Next
API route entry files. Native services are listed below.

The 24 app `/api/cron/*` entry files are included in the source census. Manually
checked cron families require configured `CRON_SECRET`/`VERCEL_CRON_SECRET`
Bearer before work. Examples: Hive `apps/hive/src/app/api/cron/hive/simulate/route.ts:14`,
Calendar provider sync `apps/calendar/src/app/api/cron/calendar/provider-sync/route.ts:45`,
Tasks cleanup `apps/tasks/src/app/api/cron/tasks/cleanup-media/route.ts:14`, Web
deadline reminders `apps/web/src/app/api/cron/tasks/deadline-reminders/route.ts:107`.
Some Pay/Inventory handlers bypass secret checks only under DEV_MODE; source
production defaults must remain intact. Existing orchestration ownership belongs
to Cloudflare and should not be expanded onto new Vercel/Supabase schedulers.

## Source-grounded gaps and breakage risks

These are review candidates, not deployment exploit claims. No live exposure or
credential configuration was tested. Do not assign severity from source alone.

1. **External storage demo acts with server SDK identity without caller auth.**
   `DELETE /api/storage/delete` forwards request-provided paths to
   `tuturuuu.storage.delete` without a user/session check
   (`apps/external/src/app/api/storage/delete/route.ts:4`, `:15`). Upload/share/list
   follow the same shape (`.../upload/route.ts:4`, `.../share/route.ts:4`,
   `.../list/route.ts:4`). The app proxy only invokes generic abuse/MFA guard
   (`apps/external/src/proxy.ts:5`); MFA guard allows requests with no credentials
   (`packages/utils/src/required-mfa-runtime.ts:100`). SDK default loads the
   server's API key (`packages/sdk/src/storage.ts:830`). If publicly deployed with
   a privileged API key, anonymous callers can act within that key's permissions.
   Owner: External/demo app. Minimum next step: establish whether deployed, then
   require actor/workspace authorization or remove demo endpoints from production.

2. **Playground public GET can initiate billable AI work.**
   `apps/playground/src/app/api/ai/object-generation/route.ts:27` calls
   `generateObject` with a Google model and ROOT_WORKSPACE_ID user/workspace
   (`:30`, `:33`, `:37`) without actor auth. The app proxy applies only the generic
   guard (`apps/playground/src/proxy.ts:5`), whose no-credential behavior is above.
   Owner: Playground. Deployment/model-key configuration unknown. Minimum fix:
   remove live demo or require explicit authorized actor with bounded quota; edge
   rate limiting is not a total-spend stop fence.

3. **Supermemory legacy routes fail open if key absent.**
   `apps/supermemory/src/server.js:51` returns true when API_KEY is empty. Routing
   at `:344` adds configured-key enforcement only for edit APIs. If the legacy
   service is exposed without SUPERMEMORY_API_KEY, read/add/search/forget routes
   can proceed unauthenticated. Owner: Memory service. Deployment admission and
   network isolation unknown; minimum next observation is configuration and
   ingress ownership, then fail closed for every non-health operation.

4. **AI agent adapter signature coverage remains unresolved.**
   Source config injects Discord publicKey / Zalo webhookSecret and delegates to
   dynamically loaded packages. No proof of missing validation; supplier behavior,
   gateway token verification, configuration and replay semantics need an
   independent source/fixture review before a narrow webhook edge skip is enabled.

5. **Token-presence exceptions break valid callers and admit spoofed markers.**
   CLI verify/refresh and pairing carry secrets in JSON; WebSockets use query
   tickets; internal browser app sessions can use cookies. Conversely, staged CI
   intentionally sends an invalid Bearer. A skip based only on Authorization
   presence is neither auth proof nor a complete machine classifier.

6. **Broad browser protection breaks machine paths outside `/api/`.**
   Meet/control/realtime/extraction/memory paths above must be explicit machine
   predicates. Returning HTML challenges to SSE/WebSocket/API traffic breaks the
   transport before origin can validate its token. Browser-path policy should
   also preserve public discovery/static metadata needed by legitimate crawlers.

7. **Existing probes cannot qualify for a secret-header exception yet.**
   CI probe supplies an intentionally invalid origin Bearer and no dedicated edge
   probe secret (`scripts/ci/verify-staged-critical-app.js:72`). The observed curl
   UA is transport identity, not authority. Introduce a narrowly scoped rotated
   secret header separately; never grant UA/IP-only skip or rewrite origin auth.

8. **Legacy query cron secret broadens accidental disclosure.**
   Discord supports `?secret=` (`apps/discord/app.py:883`), which can land in URL
   logs. No secret value was read. Prefer header-only new callers, migrate old
   callers, then remove query compatibility with explicit owner acceptance.

9. **563 route auth classifications and live host bindings remain unknown.**
   This is a coverage limitation, not 563 vulnerabilities. Keep all proposal rules
   disabled/review-only until the relevant endpoint's owner resolves origin auth,
   per-token quota behavior and application envelopes. Do not turn a census signal
   into a blanket managed-WAF/security bypass.

## Snapshot joins and limits

Each route record joins its source host candidate to the [DNS snapshot](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/blob/main/infra/cloudflare/edge-security/inventory/hosts.json). A missing host or a custom domain remains unknown. App aliases are listed separately and do not inherit a verified proxy state from the primary host. [Traffic and security settings](/build/devops/edge-security-traffic) contain the observed provider coverage. The [proposal](/build/devops/edge-security) keeps Finance and unknown service hosts outside its selectors. No deployed endpoint was tested by this source pass.

## Discovery and authentication redirects

App `public/robots.txt` and selected `public/sitemap.xml` files, plus Web `src/app/robots.ts`, `sitemap.ts`, and `manifest.ts`, are discovery endpoints used without an app session. Web proxy exclusions also reserve `/.well-known`, `site.webmanifest`, `manifest.webmanifest`, and `sw.js` (`apps/web/src/proxy.ts:1460`). The proposal preserves these transport classes and static `/_next/` requests. Colab `/auth/login` and `/auth/callback` are central-auth redirects and token redemption (`apps/colab/src/server/auth.ts:104`, `:132`). Only these exact auth redirect paths on Colab are selected; a future `/auth/register` page keeps browser protection. Actual deep-link/domain-verification files and unresolved host bindings still require owner acceptance.

The [review readiness amendment](/build/devops/edge-security#client-429-acceptance-is-still-required) records actual Dart/CLI 429 source behavior, the Hive page/socket mapping and remaining runtime acceptance. Separate lanes own the three source findings; this proposal does not fix or redeploy them.

The [app-owned header inventory](/build/devops/edge-security-headers) joins intended XFO/CSP framing with live proxied responses and records the managed-transform end state. Retained Next policy is not proof that native Meet applies it; unknown runtime/storage ownership remains open. Server self-origin maintenance and recurring QR/MFA polling are separately classified in the [readiness gates](/build/devops/edge-security#shared-refresh-and-polling-must-not-use-the-login-attempt-counter).
